title: Vintage Gibson ES-330 Value Guide: Annual Price Ranges
description: Vintage Gibson ES-330 values from 1959 to 1972, with annual price references, condition notes, P-90 pickup context and photographs from my guitar archive.
alt: Sunburst 1959 ES-330 body with black dogear pickups and a trapeze tailpiece

faqs.q: How Much Is A Vintage Gibson ES-330 Worth?
faqs.a: An excellent, original two-pickup 1959 to 1962 dot-neck ES-330 in sunburst or cherry has a guide range of $8,500 to $11,000. Standard-finish 1966 to 1972 examples sit at $5,000 to $6,000. The ranges assume the original case and aren't guaranteed offers.

faqs.q: Why Does The Annual Table End In 1972?
faqs.a: The original ES-330TD run covered here ends in 1972. Later reissues need their own appraisals. I don't extend the original-production table through 1979.

faqs.q: Is An ES-330 Worth The Same As An ES-335?
faqs.a: They use different construction and pickups. The vintage ES-330 is fully hollow and uses P-90 pickups, while the ES-335 has a center block and humbuckers. I compare each guitar within its own model and era.

faqs.q: Does A Metal Pickup Cover Mean It Has Humbuckers?
faqs.a: No. Vintage ES-330 P-90 pickups can have black or metal dogear covers. A cover alone doesn't establish the pickup's originality or the guitar's year. Replaced covers should be documented.

faqs.q: Does A Factory Bigsby Have A Fixed Premium?
faqs.a: I haven't assigned a fixed premium. A factory vibrato, a later addition and a removed unit with extra holes are different configurations. The appraisal needs to establish which one the guitar has.

faqs.q: Can A Refretted ES-330 Still Be All Original?
faqs.a: A quality refret preserves the all-original classification of an otherwise original guitar under this site's grading approach. It removes museum-quality status. Repairs, neck reshaping and replacement parts are assessed separately.
